question: Which p65 3.100.043 VFS entries does the staged loader need, and do they behave as NuttX open/close/read from an NSH exec context?
prototype_hypothesis: The ported close record (0x1c154c40) is wrong; the exact entry is the one the VFS syscall table publishes between open and read.
callsite_evidence: The table at 0xc4a96c4 holds, in order, 0x1c1580e5 (open), 0x1c154d9d, 0x1c158721 (read), 0x1c159a2d; open and read are independently recovered NuttX entries, so the second slot is close.
Mirage p65 device p65-canopus-test: open('/data/canopus/stage2.bin', 1) from an NSH exec stub returns fd 3; close at 0x1c154d9d returns 0; a second close on the same fd returns -1 (EBADF).
Calling the previously ported 0x1c154c40 with the same fd resets the emulated device, so the ported address is not close on this image.
control_flow_evidence: read(fd, buf, 64) at 0x1c158720 returns 0x40 with the first bytes of stage2.bin in the buffer.
ownership_analysis: No ownership claimed; the probe runs from the same unassigned cave 0x2019e800 the loader uses.
unsafe_assumptions: Emulator evidence only (host/emulator level); no physical device has run this.
The VFS table is read from the image, not from a live symbol table; a table relocation would invalidate it.
Only open/close/read were probed; write remains unprobed.
recommended_probe: Re-run the staged loader end to end on a Mirage p65 device and confirm /dev/canopus appears.
